newsitem.title: MACAU: Bullet-proof vest sales surge in Macau.
newsitem.headline: Bullet-proof vest sales surge in Macau.

text.p: The gangland crime wave sweeping Macau has prompted a run on bullet-proof vests, said trader Chau Tak-on.

Chau, who also sells wine and hi fi sets, he had sold 20 of his "Top Line" line of U.S.-manufacturered bullet-proof vests in the past few months comapred with his usual sales of only one or two a month.
He had only one old-fashioned model left in stock and had ordered more to meet demand.
Most of his clients were policemen, he said. Others were businessmen "worried about their personal safety."
Two or three women had also bought the vests, which retail at about US$1,035 each.
A wave of shootings, bombings and arson attacks in recent months has shocked once-sleepy Macau, located just 60 km (40 miles) east of Hong Kong.

Police blame a turf war between members of rival Chinese secret societies known as "triad societies" fighting a turf war over casino-related loansharking, smuggling, protection rackets and prostitution.

Competition has intensified as Macau's economy, particularly its property sector, suffered a downturn. Police said criminals from fast developing southern China were also trickling across Macau's porous border to seek part of the action.

Macau, a tiny 21 sq km (eight sq mile) territory of just 450,000 people, experienced a 19.4 percent rise in crime last year. Crime rose 20 percent in 1995, government figures show. A Portuguese toehold in Asia for more than 400 years, it reverts to China in December 1999.
